items.label: Research Theme 01
items.title: Early Disease Diagnosis Based on Raman Spectroscopy
items.description:
Modern medical research is rapidly shifting from treatment-centered approaches toward prevention and early diagnosis. Because appropriate therapeutic strategies depend heavily on the type and stage of a disease, the importance of early detection is increasingly emphasized.
Raman spectroscopy is an optical technique that analyzes molecular structures based on unique vibrational spectra, enabling qualitative and quantitative analysis of target analytes, and is gaining wide adoption in biomedical fields. Our laboratory develops Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) platforms and applies advanced signal analysis methods to accurately distinguish cancerous cells from normal cells. Through this research, we aim to realize rapid, accurate, and non-invasive or minimally invasive technologies for early cancer diagnosis.

items.label: Research Theme 02
items.title: Biomolecular Detection Using Ultra-Sensitive Plasmonic Sensors
items.description:
This research aims to enhance the sensitivity of conventional plasmonic sensor substrates by integrating diverse dielectric and metallic nanostructures, and to apply these platforms to the detection of highly pathogenic viruses.
By coupling nanostructures, we increase the effective sensing surface area and induce Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) and electromagnetic hot-spots, significantly boosting detection sensitivity. Building upon this technological expertise, we have successfully detected DNA amplification of avian influenza viruses and plan to expand our diagnostic capabilities to various infectious diseases, including foot-and-mouth disease and swine influenza.

items.label: Research Theme 03
items.title: Optical Detection of Neural Signals and Study of Neural Activity Mechanisms
items.description:
This research focuses on developing optical technologies to detect neural signals using plasmonic optical sensors rather than conventional electrical methods. By integrating optical sensing systems with electrical or ultrasonic stimulation, signals generated from neural cells and tissues can be measured non-invasively.
Furthermore, by developing optical neuromodulation systems capable of selectively stimulating and recording targeted neural regions, we investigate and control the underlying mechanisms of neural activity.
